summary: This video documents a field-to-post workflow for dramatic, multi-layer landscape imagery. The presenter walks through techniques to recover dynamic range, sculpt dimensionality with directional light, and build complex composites from foreground and background layers. Core methods include dodging to create directional light, selective color and white balance adjustments, and tonal-based color adjustments, all while acknowledging the challenges of processing in bright daylight. The workflow emphasizes shooting for unseen layers, careful cropping for pano-format scenes, and organizing shots into foreground/background zones. When possible, the instructor demonstrates beam creation using dehaze and targeted painting, discusses the use of camera calibration (Blue-Gold), and covers focus stacking attempts, edge separation, and flare management. The session also touches on practical constraints (tripod stability, shot alignment) and the occasional need for AI-based denoising and HDR-like processing to achieve a dramatic, multi-layer landscape.
